purpose: Teach: 一体化/つとめ/マネージメント/結集/少人数/樹立/取り込ん/交互

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: 当社の部門を一体化させましょう
lines.style: Crisp, authoritative opening. Clear enunciation on each phrase. Professional pace, no hesitation. Voice carries quiet confidence and strategic intent.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい。当社のおつとめを丁寧に果たします
lines.en: Yes. We'll handle our responsibilities with care.
lines.style: Steady, measured affirmation. Respectful but not obsequious. Weight on 「丁寧に」 — showing he takes the commitment seriously. Slight nod in the voice.

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: 現場のマネージメントを磨きましょう
lines.en: And let's sharpen our site management.
lines.style: Forward momentum. Slight lift on the opening — building on agreement. Concrete and purposeful. The cadence of someone moving from one item to the next.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい。新規プロジェクトに人材を結集させます
lines.en: Yes. We'll consolidate talent for the new project.
lines.style: Engaged and proactive. Faster pace than before — he's energised by the direction. Crisp consonants. Shows he's already thinking ahead.

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: 少人数のスタジオで企画を進めましょう
lines.en: We'll move the planning forward in a lean studio setup.
lines.style: Controlled enthusiasm. Clear syllable separation. Deliberate pacing on the key phrase. The voice of someone solving problems as she speaks.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい。新ブランドの樹立を計画します
lines.en: Yes. We'll plan the new brand launch.
lines.style: Energised agreement. Slightly quicker tempo. Confidence building through the line. On 「樹立」 — firm, like planting a flag.

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: 海外顧客の声を取り込んでいきましょう
lines.en: We need to listen to our overseas customers.
lines.style: Inclusive and strategic. Softer attack than the directives — this is about listening, not commanding. Warm urgency. Eye-level tone.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい。担当を交互に変えていきます
lines.en: Yes. We'll rotate who handles each account.
lines.style: Closing affirmation. Steady, resolved. Slight slow on the final thought — showing this closes a chapter and opens the next. Professional closure.
